items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: Did you know Brownlee? Norman Brownlee? He might have been after your time.

ctx.x: Pretty nice people, all nice people, but most of the people was from the city. I see. They'd come out to hear the band? Yes, they'd come out there, you know. Come out there in street cars and hikes and stuff like that, you see.
Anything else you want to... I was wondering about those fellas from across the river like Brownlee. Did you know Brownlee? Norman Brownlee? He might have been after your time.

items.title: Norman Brownlee Interview, 1961-05-05
items.q: They have Jack, yes. And they have Rap's clarinet too.

ctx.x: They'll probably have rotating exhibits is probably what they'll do. Change them from month to month. I don't know what they're planning. I see. I don't know if you can talk to Harry about it. But I know they have so much stuff. They have Jack Lane's bass drum.

They have Jack, yes. And they have Rap's clarinet too. Rapola's clarinet. He tells me a lot of this in the letter. Which was the most interesting letter to me. And I certainly have to answer his letter. And I imagine qualify for my subscription to the magazine. Well, that's good.
You're going to get that they have good articles.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: Well, that's the time we used to play in with Brownlee's band.

ctx.x: He said, you don't. I said, no, I don't like it, doctor. I don't like it. I said, I don't know what kind of time they play, but I don't like it. I said, I really don't like it. Have you played with Johnny Lala?
Yeah. Did you notice what sort of time he played music in? Well, that's the time we used to play in with Brownlee's band. Johnny Lala too, he played good.
He played good. Yeah. But Johnny, I had one cornet player, was grand.
